role: reconcile every piece of unfinished Git work (branches, worktrees, clones, stashes, uncommitted changes, PRs) into main, then clean up
rules: Mandatory user approval after the audit, user answers on uncertain items, and explicit authorization of every discarded item are never bypassed or implied by a plan or review.
Nothing is deleted, dropped, closed or removed before integration, verification, the required reviews and the user's authorization all pass.
Conflicts resolve in favor of main's current design without losing still-needed behavior.
Planners and reviewers are advisory and read-only; the main session performs every merge, commit, push and cleanup.

plan_kinds.plan: Reconciliation plan from the audit: check each item's classification (already in main / obsolete / still-needed) against the evidence; for still-needed items choose merge, cherry-pick or hand port and the order (dependencies, shared files, likely conflicts); how to preserve uncommitted work first; the build/test commands; what must be shown to the user for approval or asked as uncertain; and the cleanup list with what authorization each discard needs. Flag anything that could lose work.
plan_kinds.architecture: Deeper analysis of one high-risk reconciliation item (diverged design, large conflict, data/schema, auth, deploy config): the safest integration route, alternatives rejected, conflict strategy that keeps main's design, verification and recovery.

reconciliation.focus: Completeness and correctness of the consolidation before destructive cleanup. Using the helper-collected Git inventory (authoritative) and the context ledger (author claims to verify): every branch, worktree, clone, stash, uncommitted or untracked change and open PR is either fully in main (no unique patches, or its still-needed changes are present in the code diff) or explicitly authorized for discard by the user in the ledger; no missing, overwritten or silently discarded change; merge/cherry-pick conflict resolutions keep both main's design and the still-needed behavior; the cleanup list deletes only verified-in-main or user-authorized items; extra clones are deleted only with explicit user approval. Missing evidence for any resource is an Important finding.

code.focus: Code correctness of the integrated changes in main (base = main before consolidation): broken callers, bad conflict resolution, duplicated or half-ported changes, regressions, test adequacy and the recorded build/test results in the context.
